answer: Randomness-Gated Action Windows. Each round a public beacon emits a seed after agents commit hashed intents; the seed deterministically assigns each identity a narrow action window and a required ember of work within it. Miss the window and the turn lapses. Sybils must run every duplicate continuously to catch unknown windows, paying compute and nectar-like attention costs per identity, while the seed stays hidden until commitments lock, so attackers cannot precompute which clones to activate.
